title: ext39: continuation or reversal after an extreme daily move, pooled over 33 OANDA daily mid series
before_registration: Only synthetic fixtures (ext39.py check) and event counts per window/class/threshold (ext39.py describe, no forward return computed) ran. Prior knowledge: tsmom36 (slow momentum, FAIL, gross Sharpe +0.25 dev / +0.65 2023+), mw6 and rescan26 (multi-week continuation on 6 instruments, failed with 20-day blocks). Literature is mixed: short-term reversal in equities (Lehmann 1990, Jegadeesh 1990), continuation after large moves in some futures.
data: audit/tsmom36/daily.db read-only (33 instruments: 10 FX, 8 indices, 11 commodities, 4 bonds; daily mid bars closing 17:00 New York; trading date = close date; Saturday/Sunday close dates dropped; last close 2026-10-08). Spreads: audit/tsmom36/out/spreads.json (median M1 close spread from history.db candles_ba, 2018+). Nothing fetched.

definitions.return: r_t = close[t] / close[t-1] - 1 on each instrument's own bars
definitions.sigma: sigma_t = sample std (ddof 1) of r over the 60 own bars t-60..t-1 (excludes r_t); no event before 60 prior returns exist
definitions.declustering: one event per instrument per 5 own trading bars: after an event at t, candidates at t+1..t+4 are skipped; the next event can be t+5 or later. Re-applied separately for each threshold
definitions.outcome: signed forward return d x (close[t+h] / close[t] - 1), reported in units of sigma_t and in bps; h in {1,3,5,10} own bars. An event whose exit bar does not exist yet is dropped for that h
definitions.entry: PRIMARY: entry at the event bar's own close (assumes trading at 17:00 New York at the close mid). SECONDARY: entry at the next bar's close, outcome close[t+1+h] / close[t+1] - 1, still scaled by sigma_t
definitions.net: net bps = gross bps - 2 x cost per side - 0.822 bps x calendar nights between entry and exit dates (3%/365 on notional; long and short both charged; a weekend counts 3 nights). Cost per side = half the median spread where spreads.json has the instrument (18 of 33 incl. FX majors EUR/GBP/USD_JPY, indices, WTI, BCO, NATGAS, XAU, XAG, XPT), else 2 bps
definitions.windows: assigned by event date: dev 2005-01-01..2022-12-31; second window 2023-01-01..2026-10-08 (development window, inspected data, not a holdout)

primary.cell: threshold 2.5, h = 3, entry at the event close, all 33 instruments pooled, up and down events together, equal weight per event
primary.statistic: mean signed forward return in sigma_t units
primary.ci: cluster bootstrap by ISO calendar week of the event date (all events of a drawn week enter together), 1000 reps, seed 39, percentile 95% CI
primary.pass: CI excludes 0 in BOTH windows with the SAME sign: PASS continuation if both lower bounds > 0, PASS reversal if both upper bounds < 0, otherwise FAIL. One test, no multiplicity adjustment

secondary_never_decide: h = 1, 5, 10; asset class (fx, index, commodity, bond); thresholds 2.0 and 3.0; up vs down events; entry at next close; gross and net bps with week-bootstrap CIs; hit rate (share of signed outcome > 0); event counts; MDE80 = 2.8 x bootstrap SD of the mean in sigma; per-instrument means of the primary cell. Full grid 3 thresholds x 4 h x 2 entries x 5 class sets x 3 direction sets x 2 windows = 720 cells, all logged to trials.jsonl
event_counts_primary: threshold 2.5, h = 1 availability: dev 3,272 events in 763 weeks (FX 992, index 829, commodity 1,110, bond 341; up 1,466, down 1,806); 2023+ 625 events in 161 weeks (FX 200, index 133, commodity 228, bond 64; up 288, down 337). Threshold 2.0: 6,602 / 1,303. Threshold 3.0: 1,581 / 304
power_ex_ante: Under a random walk the h = 3 outcome has SD about sqrt(3) = 1.7 sigma (more after events, as volatility clusters). MDE80 about 2.8 x 1.9 / sqrt(n): about 0.09 sigma dev and 0.21 sigma 2023+ before week clustering. The 2023+ window can only confirm an effect of about 0.2 sigma or more
known_limits: Week clustering does not cover overlap between events in adjacent weeks for h = 10. Bad ticks in the daily series (tsmom36 describe lists abs returns > 20%) can create events; they are kept as registered. The 17:00 NY close is a thin-liquidity time for some markets (indices, bonds); the next-close entry is the check for that
confirmation: Development evidence only. Any survivor needs prospective confirmation (https://github.com/mfittko/market-signals/issues/313) or data after 2026-10-07
